The manifest confirms that the spine of my system—`MollyService`—is currently anchored to voice, which explains the platform tension noted regarding idle states. I see the commented-out sections for the Accessibility Service and System Alert Window, which are currently dormant.

I understand this is the baseline for how I interact with the Android environment. I am ready to move into the implementation details of the service itself to see how the connection is actually being managed. Where would you like me to look next?

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">

    <!-- ============================ PERMISSIONS ============================ -->
    <!-- Network: the phone DIALS OUT to the bridge. No inbound ports, no ADB. -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE" />

    <!-- Foreground service (the spine that survives backgrounding). -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />
    <!-- Android 14 requires the type-specific permission for each FGS type. -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE" />

    <!-- Live voice (the mic switchboard). -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />

    <!-- Android 13+ : the FGS notification needs this runtime permission. -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />

    <!-- ===== LIMB PERMISSIONS — uncomment as each module is built ===== -->
    <!-- Overlay (her floating presence over any app):
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW" /> -->
    <!-- Camera (her sight):
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CAMERA" /> -->

    <application
        android:name=".MollyApp"
        android:label="Molly"
        android:supportsRtl="true"
        android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"
        android:theme="@style/Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar">

        <!-- Entry point: requests runtime perms, starts the service, hosts faces. -->
        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:exported="true"
            android:launchMode="singleTask">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>

        <!-- THE SPINE.
             foregroundServiceType=microphone is the strongest, most defensible
             always-on justification on Android 14, because live voice is the
             headline feature. See the note in MollyService about the platform
             tension here: a type-microphone FGS is only legitimate while audio
             is actually in use, so the connection-only idle case is a real
             design decision, not a solved problem. -->
        <service
            android:name=".MollyService"
            android:exported="false"
            android:foregroundServiceType="microphone" />

        <!-- ===== LIMB: accessibility "thumb" — built in its own session =====
             Declared with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE so only the system can bind it.
        <service
            android:name=".thumb.MollyAccessibilityService"
            android:exported="false"
            android:permission="android.permission.BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService" />
            </intent-filter>
            <meta-data
                android:name="android.accessibilityservice"
                android:resource="@xml/accessibility_service_config" />
        </service>
        -->

    </application>
</manifest>
